newsitem.title: GERMANY: Move out of soy oil seen possible in gene soya row.
newsitem.headline: Move out of soy oil seen possible in gene soya row.

text.p: EU processors may cut soy oil use amid uncertainty over the impact of a campaign launched by Greenpeace in Germany, the Oil World newsletter said.

The independent publication said the situation was hard to gauge but some processors of margarine and other secondary products may reduce, or temporarily abandon, soy oil use as long as the likely consumer response was still uncertain.
A shift in demand from soya oil to rape, sunseed and palm oils could have a major impact on prices.
Fob mill Rotterdam rapeoil -- usually at a discount to soy oil -- last week moved to a premium.
The Nov/Jan premium was today 5.25 guilders per 100 kilos, with rape oil at 100.50 guilders in the three delivery months.
Greenpeace earlier this month said it would mobilise consumer protests against genetically altered U.S. soybean imports, which are due for arrival in late 1996.
Oil World said if soy oil fell out of favour, EU rape oil supplies could become tight in the 1996/97 season as domestic rapeseed crops had been lower and generated lower oil content.
While this could benefit sun and palm oil consumption, EU rape oil exports could also decline and non-food rape oil switched back into food uses.
